issues.legal_issue: A plaint seeking specific performance over immovable property must describe the property sufficiently for it to be identified, and the trial court must require an adequate description where the plaint does not do so.
material_facts: The suit concerned part of a larger revenue plot, but the sub-plot numbers used in the parties’ title documents did not appear in the revenue records or survey map.
The property could not be identified merely by the stated sub-plot numbers or boundaries.
The plaint contained no map of the suit property, and the trial court nevertheless decreed the suit.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs should have filed a map of the property, and the trial court should have noticed the omission and required one before proceeding with the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Order 7 Rule 3 CPC requires a plaint concerning immovable property to describe it sufficiently to identify it and, where identification is possible by boundaries or numbers in survey or settlement records, to specify them. This enables a proper decree under Order 20 Rule 3 CPC. No earlier cases are relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: suit_concerns_immovable_property and property_not_identifiable_from_boundaries_or_survey_records and plaint_lacks_identifying_map and trial_court_decreed_suit

predicates.suit_concerns_immovable_property: The proceeding seeks relief concerning a particular item of immovable property.
predicates.property_not_identifiable_from_boundarie: The property cannot be identified from its stated boundaries or numbers in the applicable survey or settlement records.
predicates.plaint_lacks_identifying_map: The plaintiff did not include a map sufficient to identify the property in the plaint.
predicates.trial_court_decreed_suit: The trial court entered a decree despite the inadequate property description.

issues.definition: When a suit concerns immovable property that cannot be identified from the stated boundaries or survey records and the plaint lacks an identifying map, the trial court must require an adequate description before decreeing the suit.

issues.legal_issue: An uncertain description of property in a decree may be resolved in execution, and an accidental omission or error in the record may be corrected so that the decree can be given effect.
material_facts: The decree for specific performance referred to the suit lands but had no accompanying map.
A map was first filed during execution as part of a draft sale deed, and the map in the executed sale deed differed in some respects from the maps attached to the judgment-debtors’ title deeds.
The sub-plot numbers were not shown in the revenue records, and possession had not been delivered to the decree-holders.
The existing title documents, revenue records and maps could assist in identifying the land intended to be sold.
issues.conclusion: The executing court must hear the parties and determine whether the map in the court sale deed correctly identifies the decretal property; it may correct the map and sale deed if necessary, then deliver the identified property to the decree-holders.
issues.legal_principle: Where a decree for immovable property does not identify the property definitely, the defect may be cured under Section 152 CPC if it is an inadvertent error not affecting the merits, or the property may be ascertained as a question concerning execution, discharge or satisfaction under Section 47 CPC. In this case, the Court considered Section 47 more appropriate. A decree should, so far as practicable, not be defeated by an accidental slip or omission. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.execution_of_immovable_property_decree: The proceeding is execution of a decree concerning immovable property.
predicates.decretal_property_is_not_definitely_iden: The decree and its record do not establish the precise identity of the property to be transferred.
predicates.execution_documents_contain_uncertain_or: A map used during execution is uncertain or differs from relevant maps in the title documents.
predicates.possession_has_not_been_delivered: The decree-holder has not yet obtained possession of the property under the decree.

issues.definition: When execution concerns immovable property whose identity is uncertain, execution maps are uncertain or discrepant, and possession has not been delivered, the executing court must establish the property’s identity and correct the execution documents if needed before delivering possession.

issues.legal_issue: A draft document submitted for execution of a decree must be served on the judgment-debtor with an opportunity to object, and the court must determine any objections before approving the draft.
material_facts: The decree required execution and registration of a sale deed.
The decree-holders submitted a draft sale deed with a map during execution.
The court did not serve the draft with a notice requiring objections, and the judgment-debtors repeatedly sought delivery of the draft so they could object.
The executing court did not determine whether the property shown in the draft map was the property covered by the agreement and decree.
issues.conclusion: The prescribed notice and determination of objections had not occurred; the executing court must hear the parties and decide the correctness of the map, making any necessary correction to the sale deed.
issues.legal_principle: Order 21 Rule 34 CPC provides that where a decree requires execution of a document, the decree-holder may submit a draft; the court must serve it on the judgment-debtor with notice to make objections, determine any objections made, and approve or alter the draft consistently with its determination. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.execution_requires_document_to_be_drawn: The decree requires a document to be executed as part of its enforcement.
predicates.decree_holder_submits_draft_document: The decree-holder submits a draft of the document for the court to execute or approve.
predicates.court_does_not_serve_draft_for_objection: The court fails to serve the draft on the judgment-debtor with an opportunity to object.

issues.definition: When enforcement requires a document, the decree-holder submits a draft, and the court has not served it for objections, the court must serve the draft and determine objections before approving it.

issues.legal_issue: Security deposited to obtain a stay of execution cannot be appropriated for the benefit of the opposing party without a final judicial order authorizing that appropriation.
material_facts: During an appeal from the decree, the judgment-debtors deposited money as security for a stay of execution.
The interim order allowed the opposing parties to withdraw the security on furnishing security of their own.
The security was withdrawn by the judgment-debtors, and the appellate court made no final order forfeiting it or applying it to costs or mesne profits.
issues.conclusion: The security could not be appropriated by the decree-holders and had to be returned to the judgment-debtors; the decree-holders were directed to deposit the corresponding amount for payment to the judgment-debtors.
issues.legal_principle: The Court referred to the power under Order 41 Rule 6 CPC in connection with security for a stay pending appeal. In the absence of a final judicial order forfeiting the security or applying it to another liability, the deposited security remains returnable to the person who deposited it. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.appeal_includes_stay_of_execution: The proceeding is an appeal in which execution of a decree is stayed.
predicates.judgment_debtor_deposits_security_for_st: The judgment-debtor deposits money as security required for the stay.
predicates.final_order_does_not_authorize_forfeitur: The final disposition contains no judicial direction forfeiting the security or applying it to another liability.

issues.definition: When a judgment-debtor deposits security for a stay pending appeal and the final order does not authorize its forfeiture or application, the security must be returned to the depositor.
